data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"21 pencils cost $6 because the covering principle for uniform unit rates applies: 21 is a multiple of 7, so the bundle price scales by the factor 21/7 = 3, yielding 3 \u00d7 $2 = $6.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the store's pricing is strictly limited to one bundle per customer, the cost of 21 pencils is not determined by the given information.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the store imposes a non-linear bulk discount or surcharge for quantities other than exactly 7, the $6 result may not hold.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the '7 for $2' price is a limited-time or conditional promotion not applicable to a 21-pencil purchase, the $6 result is not entailed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the store refuses to sell 21 pencils at all (e.g., inventory limit), the question is unanswerable under the given data.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The stated price '7 for $2' establishes a uniform unit rate of $2/7 per pencil. When the target quantity (21) is an exact integer multiple of the bundle size (7), the covering principle directly applies: the cost is (21/7) \u00d7 $2 = 3 \u00d7 $2 = $6. No pro-ration or fractional-bundle assumption is required, so the discrete-bundle and continuous-unit-rate models converge exactly.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
